name: Primary CNS lymphoma
theme: two currencies: survival and cognition · the steroid trap

meta.title: Primary CNS lymphoma in silico decision trainer
meta.condition: Primary CNS lymphoma (immunocompetent adult), including vitreoretinal involvement
meta.population: Immunocompetent adults with primary large B-cell lymphoma of the CNS (WHO-HAEM5 groups CNS/vitreoretinal/testicular as immune-privileged-site lymphomas; ICC keeps them distinct - both cited). Median age mid-60s; the disease where treatment decisions are paid for in two currencies at once - survival AND cognition. Vitreoretinal involvement is a branch INSIDE this spec. Out of scope with visible exits: secondary CNS lymphoma (systemic disease drives - routes toward the DLBCL trainer), HIV-associated and post-transplant CNS lymphoma (own pathways; every frontline PCNSL trial excluded them).
meta.summary: Evidence-linked teaching application for the lymphoma behind the blood-brain barrier - where the biopsy gate has a chemical enemy (steroids melt the evidence), where high-dose methotrexate is the backbone no trial has dethroned, and where the great 2026 news is a randomized answer to the consolidation question: IELSG43 (Lancet, July 2026) showed thiotepa-ASCT beats non-myeloablative chemotherapy (3-yr PFS 78% vs 51%, HR 0.43). The consolidation cards render survival near-parity between ASCT and reduced-dose WBRT - and the trainer teaches that this tie breaks on NEUROCOGNITION (PRECIS at 8 yea…
meta.disclaimer: Synthetic teaching environment. Not medical advice; every number is a claim with a citation and an expiry date.
meta.classification: WHO-HAEM5 (2022) primary large B-cell lymphoma of immune-privileged sites / ICC (2022) primary DLBCL of the CNS; site-specific diagnosis on the pathology report
meta.response: IPCG response criteria (neuroimaging + corticosteroid dose + slit-lamp exam + CSF cytology - the four-part response this disease demands)

Patient.label: Age
Patient.help: The menu's biggest fork: fit patients to ~70 get the MATRix-to-ASCT road; past it, MTX-based programs without transplant. The honest registry fact rides along: elderly PCNSL outcomes have not improve…
Patient.helpPatient: This lymphoma is usually diagnosed in the 60s. Age shapes which of the strong plans is safe - and the strongest ones now reach further into older age than they used to.

Patient.label: Performance status (ECOG)
Patient.help: An IELSG factor and an MSKCC-RPA axis - but in PCNSL a poor performance status is often the LYMPHOMA talking, and can reverse dramatically with induction; the score is honest about today, not destiny.
Patient.helpPatient: How much daily life is limited right now - and in this disease, treatment itself often improves it quickly.

Disease.label: Host immune status
Disease.help: WHO-HAEM5 reserves the immune-privileged-site entity for immunocompetent hosts; HIV-associated and PTLD CNS lymphoma have their own pathways (antiretroviral optimization, immunosuppression reduction)…
Disease.helpPatient: Lymphomas that grow because the immune system is suppressed follow a different playbook - this trainer hands those off rather than guessing.

Disease.label: Disease compartments
Disease.help: Secondary CNS lymphoma is systemic lymphoma first: NCCN routes it through the B-Cell Lymphomas guideline, and none of the PCNSL trial evidence below enrolled it. The vitreoretinal branch stays - the…
Disease.helpPatient: If the lymphoma is also outside the nervous system, the body-wide disease leads the plan - that path runs through the aggressive-lymphoma trainer.

Disease.label: Histologic confirmation
Disease.help: The steroid trap: corticosteroids are lymphotoxic enough to shrink the lesion into un-diagnosability. Tissue before therapy; steroids after tissue (unless herniation risk demands otherwise - and then…
Disease.helpPatient: A brain biopsy sounds like the scary step, but it is the one that makes every good decision after it possible - and one common steroid drug, given too early, can hide the answer.

Disease.label: IELSG risk score
Disease.help: Five factors: age >60, ECOG >1, elevated LDH, high CSF protein, deep-structure involvement. The forecast instrument - it drives the posterior, not the menu.
Disease.helpPatient: A five-item score that says how hard this lymphoma tends to push back - it shapes vigilance, not the goal.

Disease.label: Transplant / intensive-consolidation candidacy
Disease.help: The 2026 randomized answer (IELSG43) belongs to the transplant-eligible; the ineligible corner is where outcomes have stalled for decades and where CAROLYN is testing frontline CAR-T.
Disease.helpPatient: Whether the strongest consolidation is safe for you - and if not, this is exactly where the newest trials are focused.

On treatment.label: End-of-induction response (IPCG)
On treatment.help: The four-part IPCG read (MRI + steroid dose + slit-lamp + CSF). Response earns consolidation - IELSG32's 7-year lesson is that consolidation converts responses into the 70%-alive stratum.
On treatment.helpPatient: The mid-plan scorecard across every compartment this lymphoma can hide in - a good one opens the strongest phase of treatment.

Relapse routing.label: Relapse pattern
Relapse routing.help: IELSG32's long follow-up found salvage largely ineffective EXCEPT late relapse re-treated with methotrexate - the calendar routes this menu too.
Relapse routing.helpPatient: How long the remission lasted decides whether the original backbone drug gets another turn.

Relapse routing.label: Prior BTK-inhibitor exposure
Relapse routing.help: The only recruiting randomized R/R trial (IGNITE) excludes prior BTK-inhibitor exposure - treatment history is trial eligibility here.
Relapse routing.helpPatient: Whether this drug family has been tried decides one card and one trial door.

Where you are.label: months since diagnosis
Where you are.help: Twin clock: places 'you are here' on the months-from-diagnosis axis. Not read by the engine (completeness_only).
Where you are.helpPatient: How long since your diagnosis - marks where you are on the modelled journey.

Newly diagnosed.name: MATRix -> thiotepa-ASCT (IELSG32/43 - the randomized road)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: NCCN CNS Cancers (PCNSL, fit/eligible) - category via current version (403 this run, secondhand)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 randomized consolidation (IELSG43) on a randomized induction winner (IELSG32)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: the menu's most intense road: MATRix cytopenias (6% toxic deaths in IELSG32), then the transplant block - traded for the best disease control AND preserved cog…
Newly diagnosed.patient: The strongest road: four intensive cycles, then a transplant using your own cells - the plan a 2026 randomized trial crowned, and the one that best protects thinking and memory.
drugs: MATRix (HD-methotrexate, cytarabine, thiotepa, rituximab) -> thiotepa/carmustine-conditioned ASCT

Newly diagnosed.name: R-MPV -> reduced-dose WBRT + cytarabine (the 23.4-Gy middle road)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: NCCN CNS Cancers (PCNSL) - category via current version (secondhand)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 2 + randomized rdWBRT support (RTOG 1114: PFS benefit, OS neutral)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: gentler than the transplant road cycle-for-cycle; the open question is decades-scale cognition at 23.4 Gy - lower dose than the 40-Gy data that scared the fiel…
Newly diagnosed.patient: Chemotherapy first, then a deliberately lowered dose of whole-brain radiation - close to the transplant road on survival, without the transplant.
drugs: R-MPV (rituximab, HD-methotrexate, procarbazine, vincristine) -> 23.4 Gy WBRT -> cytarabine

Newly diagnosed.name: MPV-A (older patients - the randomized elderly comparison's winner)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: NCCN CNS Cancers (PCNSL, older/unfit) - category via current version (secondhand)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: HD-MTX logistics dominate; dose-flexed cycle by cycle on renal function and recovery
Newly diagnosed.patient: The full-intent chemotherapy program built and tested specifically in older patients - the goal is still lasting remission.

Newly diagnosed.name: R-MP (PRIMAIN - the gentler elderly program)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: NCCN CNS Cancers (PCNSL, older/unfit) - category via current version (secondhand)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: the lightest MTX-based program on the menu; still an admission-based backbone
Newly diagnosed.patient: A lighter version of the backbone program, proven in patients over 65 - built for finishing, not just starting.

Newly diagnosed.name: WBRT alone (the pre-methotrexate era, kept honest)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: reserved for MTX-impossible situations per guideline practice (secondhand)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: rapid response, short remission, and at historical doses a heavy delayed neurotoxicity ledger
Newly diagnosed.patient: Radiation alone works fast and does not hold long - it is the road when chemotherapy truly is not possible, and the number it shows is the honest one.

Newly diagnosed.name: Comfort-focused care
Newly diagnosed.guideline: always on the menu, never by drift
Newly diagnosed.evidence: historical series (teaching estimate, flagged); palliative-care integration randomized
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: none from antitumor therapy; neurologic symptom management is the whole craft
Newly diagnosed.patient: Declining treatment in this disease means a short road, made as comfortable as skill allows - the card says so plainly because the choice deserves the truth.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: HD-MTX re-challenge (late relapse - the one endorsed salvage)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: NCCN CNS Cancers (late relapse) - category via current version (secondhand)
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: the familiar MTX logistics, again - and this time the consolidation question reopens for those who never had it
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: A remission that held a year or more means the original backbone drug has earned another turn - the one relapse road with long-run evidence behind it.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Ibrutinib (BTK inhibition - phase 1/2 honest)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: NCCN CNS Cancers (R/R) - category via current version (secondhand)
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: phase 1/2 single-arm (no randomized evidence - IGNITE is running)
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: bruising, atrial-fibrillation vigilance - and invasive aspergillosis as the CNS-context warning, steroid-amplified
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: A daily capsule that crosses into the brain and works in about half of patients - honestly briefly on its own, which is why the randomized trial testing its cousin is on the trial screen.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Lenalidomide + rituximab (REVRI)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: NCCN CNS Cancers (R/R) - category via current version (secondhand)
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: cytopenias and rash; REMS pregnancy program; outpatient rhythm
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: A capsule-plus-antibody combination with real responses in a third of patients - an outpatient road when the intensive ones are spent.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: CAR-T (tisa-cel pilot; axi-cel's PCNSL exclusion removed 2026-02)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: emerging option (label-permitted since 2026-02 for axi-cel); trial enrollment preferred where open
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: phase 1/2 pilot (n=12) + label change; nothing randomized
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: CRS/ICANS with dedicated neuro-monitoring - in the pilot, milder than the field feared
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: Re-engineered immune cells, now formally open to this disease: in the first careful study, half of patients reached complete remission and the feared brain toxicity stayed mild.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Comfort-focused care
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: always on the menu, never by drift
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: Choosing comfort with symptoms managed well - a real chapter, entered deliberately, with the neurologic care that this disease specifically needs.

milestones.title: Biopsy BEFORE steroids when safe
review: BIOPSY BEFORE STEROIDS when safe - steroids melt the target and cost the diagnosis
fitness + age route the induction (MATRix-to-ASCT for the fit; MPV-A/R-MP ladder for the elderly; the elderly curve has not moved in 40 years - firsthand)
consolidation is decided by COGNITION as much as PFS (IELSG32 7-yr: WBRT and ASCT tie on efficacy, diverge on minds; IELSG43 crowned ASCT in the fit)
at relapse: the interval licenses methotrexate rechallenge; ibrutinib bridges; CAR-T's exclusion era is over (12-patient proof)

El-Jawahri A, LeBlanc T, VanDusen H, et al. Effect of Inpatient Palliative Care on Quality of Life 2 Weeks After Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation: A Randomized Clinical Trial. JAMA 2016;316(20):2094-2103 (PMID 27893130, NCT02207322) — abstract read firsthand 2026-09-10. POPULATION CAUTION, added at that read because the previous label named no population at all: this is a SINGLE-INSTITUTION randomized trial of 160 adults with HAEMATOLOGICAL malignancy hospitalized for autologous or allogeneic stem-cell transplantation, and its outcomes are quality of life, depression, anxiety, fatigue and symptom burden — it reports no survival and no adverse-event table. It is the factory's standing anchor for the PRINCIPLE that palliative care runs alongside active treatment rather than after it; it is not evidence in this tumour type and is not the source of any number on this card.

HBV SCREENING (the reactivation law): Hwang et al., 'Hepatitis B Virus Screening and Management for Patients With Cancer Prior to Therapy: ASCO Provisional Clinical Opinion Update' (J Clin Oncol 2020;38:3698-3715 - PMID 32716741, pubmed-eutils abstract read 2026-08-27): ALL patients anticipating systemic anticancer therapy tested with 3 tests (HBsAg, anti-HBc total Ig/IgG, anti-HBs) WITHOUT delaying therapy. Chronic HBV (HBsAg+): antiviral prophylaxis through and >=12 months after therapy. Past HBV (HBsAg-/anti-HBc+) + HIGH-RISK therapy (anti-CD20 antibodies, SCT): prophylaxis during and >=12 months after; monitoring only as an adherence-dependent alternative.

honesty: Unverified statuses never carry the current date; every 'confirm' lives in the manifest staleness list.

The consolidation fork is a two-currency decision and renders as one: ASCT and reduced-dose-WBRT roads show survival within 2 per-100 of each other (property-enforced), and the tie-breaking evidence - PRECIS at 8 years:…

IELSG43's randomized answer (ASCT 3-yr PFS 78% vs 51% over non-myeloablative chemo, HR 0.43) is quoted from the Lancet 2026 paper; its 3-yr OS point values remain conference-derived and are flagged as such on the card.
The rituximab paradox is taught as unresolved: HOVON 105 (randomized, HR 1.00) beside IELSG32's 7-year arm-B trend - the trainer does not pick a winner the field has not picked.
The steroid trap renders at the biopsy gate: tissue before dexamethasone when safety allows, because steroids can melt the evidence - an order-of-operations lesson no menu should bury.

The R/R shelf is phase-1/2 honest: ibrutinib, lenalidomide-rituximab, and CAR-T display response endpoints at their true evidence weight (n=52, n=50, n=12), none of them rank, and the axi-cel label milestone is presente…

The elderly truth is stated: population outcomes for patients over 70 have not improved in four decades (Mendez) - which is why the transplant-ineligible corner routes loudly to CAROLYN and the trial screen.
Alliance 51101's lesson is carried verbatim: the ITT analysis favored ASCT and the consolidation-landmark analysis did not - WHEN you measure changes WHAT you conclude, and the card says so.
